rounds.text: Mazda Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 15.9x [E1], which is a significant discount compared to the sector benchmark P/E of 27.45x [E6], offering investors a compelling valuation entry point. The company is in an exceptionally robust financial position with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and Rs 0 Cr in borrowings, making it practically debt-free [E38, E39, E59]. Furthermore, intrinsic value estimates derived from discounted cash flow analysis suggest a substantial margin of safety of 36.2% at the current market price of ₹ 218 [E2, E45, E46]. Fundamental operating metrics remain healthy, including a solid return on capital employed of 14.99% that outpaces the sector benchmark of 18.2% relative to peers, alongside a dependable dividend payout of 26.2% [E10, E60]. Recent operational momentum is also visible with strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 10% and profit growth of 11%, accompanied by positive institutional money flow [E17, E21, E44]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 6.83% over the past five years and negative operating and free cash flows of ₹ -19 Cr and ₹ -23 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36, E61].

Despite a zero debt structure [E38], Mazda Ltd suffers from severe operational deterioration highlighted by a collapse in cash generation, where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -19 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -23 Cr in Mar 2026 [E35, E36]. This poor cash performance translates to an alarming cash conversion ratio of -0.68x against reported profit, with operating cash flow representing only -35% of operating profit [E34, E37]. Working capital inefficiency has ballooned dramatically, evidenced by debtor days worsening from 77.4 to 102 days and overall working capital days surging from 161 days to an extreme 295 days [E63, E64]. Growth momentum has also ground to a near halt over the medium term, posting a meager 3% compounded sales growth and a stagnant 1% compounded profit growth over the last 3 years [E16, E20]. Margin compression further undermines the fundamental quality of the business, with operating margins contracting by 4 percentage points over three years down to 16% in Mar 2026 [E30], while historical returns remain low with a 3-year average ROE of 12.7% [E62]. Conceded: [E45], [E46]

Conceded: [E35], [E36], [E63], [E64]. Despite these reported cash flow and working capital strains in Mar 2026, the company remains completely debt-free at 0.00x debt-to-equity with zero borrowings of Rs 0 Cr, entirely insulating its balance sheet from solvency risk [E38, E39]. Furthermore, the bear overlooks recent operational momentum where trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 10% and profit growth hit 11% [E17, E21], supported by recent quarterly results showing a 13% YoY net profit increase and a +1 percentage point improvement in quarterly operating margin to 16% [E31, E68]. The market is overly punishing the stock based on stale sentiment, ignoring that results are improving with a strong results score of 76 out of 100 [E72]. This disconnect creates deep undervaluation, with the stock trading at a depressed P/E of 15.87x and EV/EBITDA of 10.29x compared to sector benchmarks of 27.45x and 18.02x [E6, E11]. Finally, today's depressed price implies a mere 4.8% earnings growth against the 11.0% assumed in the base case, offering an attractive margin of safety [E47].

Conceded: [E38, E39]. While the balance sheet shows zero borrowings, the complete absence of debt does not negate the severe liquidity contraction that occurred in Mar 2026, where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -19 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -23 Cr [E35, E36]. The bull highlights recent TTM growth of 10% in sales and 11% in profits [E17, E21], but ignores the multi-year stagnation where 3-year compounded sales growth is 3% and profit growth is a meager 1% [E16, E20]. Operating margins have also deteriorated by 4 percentage points over three years to 16% [E30], and the trend is explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E32, E33]. The multiple discount relative to sector benchmarks [E6, E11] is justified by ballooning working capital days expanding from 161 to 295 days and debtor days rising from 77.4 to 102 days [E63, E64]. Finally, the negative 1-year price return of -27.9% and technical positioning below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages indicate persistent structural weakness rather than merely stale sentiment [E50, E52].
